$comment: The icons contract. This file is data, not a JSON Schema meta-schema: it states the shape the consumer relies on and the token/value rules, so a mapping entry and a template can be checked against a written contract instead of against a renderer's behaviour. `schema_major` is the consumer-compatibility version (spine AD-12) and moves independently of the repo tag; raising it requires a MAJOR tag, and the validator that implements a version is bumped in the same commit as this file.

paths.note: Both roots are repo-local and relative to this repository's root. This file names no deployment path and no consumer destination (spine AD-2/AD-6). `vocabulary.json` is the role vocabulary of record and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` the reviewed role proposal; neither is a mapping file and neither is loaded by a consumer.

token_families.description: The ONLY two placeholder families. A token's family is carried by its name, and its value space follows from the family: a colour role is NOT a number and an opacity is NOT a role. Any other token name is invalid, declared or used.

COLOR.value: a role declared in `mappings/vocabulary.json`, or a `#rrggbb` literal
COLOR.note: The `#rrggbb` literal is the documented exception for brand art that must not be recoloured; it is not a palette role and the producer never resolves it.

OPACITY.value: a numeric literal in [0, 1] (1 = fully present, 0 = removed)
OPACITY.note: Emitted verbatim after the range check. `nan`, `inf`, `1_0`, a role name and anything outside 0..1 are rejected. An opacity value is a rendering parameter, never a state language of its own: adjacent bar states must differ by shape (the corpus's bluetooth rule), and the level families below dim strips that are always drawn.

token_families.syntax: {{NAME}} — exactly two opening braces, the family-prefixed name, two closing braces, no whitespace inside, nothing else on the token
rules: Every token used by any .svg under a group's template directory MUST be declared in that group's `color_mappings` (or a variant override), or in `icons/mappings/defaults.yaml` (the group-independent COLOR_* vocabulary).

Every COLOR_* value MUST be a role declared in `icons/mappings/vocabulary.json` or a `#rrggbb` literal. `colorN` carrier indices and the producer aliases (`foreground`, `accent`, `accent-muted`, `warning`) are rejected: their meaning is positional or re-mapped, not semantic. The one exception is `phase_a_legacy_baseline` in `vocabulary.json`, an exact, shrink-only list of the pre-migration values that Phase B must empty.
Every OPACITY_* value MUST be a numeric literal in [0, 1]. Assigning it a role, or assigning a number to a COLOR_* token, is a family violation, not a typo.
Declaring a token no SVG uses is allowed (forward compatibility); `make validate-icons` reports it, it does not fail the tag.
No defaults, filters, conditionals or nesting inside a token: `{{COLOR_BG|#000}}`, `{{ COLOR_BG }}` and `{{{{...}}}}` are invalid.

A token is substituted by the CONSUMER at render time. No rendered SVG, no generated icon index and no palette state is ever committed here (spine AD-11), so a preview of this corpus lives in the consumer, not in this repository.
`output` values and mapping keys may not contain `{{`: a placeholder in a destination is not renderable by any consumer.

shape.description: `icons/mappings/icons.yaml` is THE group map: a YAML document whose TOP-LEVEL KEYS are icon groups. A group is a logical name, not necessarily a directory: `battery`, `network` and `wifi-*` all live under `status-bar/`, addressed by their variant `template` paths. The only directory knob is the group's optional `template_dir`. `icons/mappings/defaults.yaml` is the exception: its top-level key is `defaults`, the group-independent COLOR_* vocabulary, not a group. No other mapping file may exist beside these two.

mapping_file.root: mapping of group name -> group entry
mapping_file.consumer: exactly one group map, `icons.yaml`, plus the vocabulary `defaults.yaml`. Per-group splitting is deliberately not supported: a consumer loads ONE mapping file, so a second group map would be a second source of truth that drifts. `make validate-icons` fails if any other `*.yaml` appears under `mappings/`. The six legacy per-concern files (battery, email-client, network, power-menu, wallpaper-selector, wlogout) were retired in v0.2.0 because they duplicated groups owned by `icons.yaml` and nothing loaded them.
mapping_file.companions: `vocabulary.json` (the declared role vocabulary) and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` (the reviewed group/variant -> role proposal) live beside the two mapping files. They are contracts and documentation, not mappings: the consumer loads neither, they carry no templates, and the `*.yaml` single-manifest rule above is unchanged. `make validate-icons` reads `vocabulary.json` as the authority for COLOR_* values and `ROLE-MIGRATION.md` as the coverage record.

group_entry.id: string — the group name; the key itself, unique within its mapping file
group_entry.template_dir: string — OPTIONAL directory under `templates_root` that variant templates are joined under; defaults to "." (the templates root itself). Must stay inside `templates_root`
group_entry.surface: string — REQUIRED; the group's default surface class: `wallpaper`, `dark-glass` or `solid`. It is the surface a bare render uses and the one whose ink the group's own `COLOR_FOREGROUND` pin must satisfy
group_entry.serves: array — OPTIONAL list of the surfaces this group serves, each one of the three classes, unique, and containing `surface`. Defaults to `[surface]`. A group that renders on more than one surface lists every surface here instead of shipping `system-*` duplicate rows; the non-default surfaces take their ink from the surface-ink contract at render time. The surface dimension is a render input: `make validate-icons` checks every surface a row actually renders on
group_entry.styles: array — OPTIONAL declared style dimension (e.g. `[default, bold, rounded]`). When present it must be unique, non-empty, and every variant MUST declare a `style` from it; when absent the group has the single implicit style `default`. A style redraws the whole state set; it never becomes part of the state vocabulary (`bar_mappings.states` stays the state -> variant table)
group_entry.color_mappings: object — OPTIONAL token map for the group: COLOR_NAME -> declared role (or `#rrggbb`), and OPACITY_NAME -> numeric literal. Group-scoped values are the defaults every variant inherits; the map is the same map the renderer merges, so both families live side by side and their names disambiguate them
group_entry.variants: array — REQUIRED, at least one; see variant_entry
group_entry.consumer_metadata: `bar_mappings`, `output_dir` and `unsafe` are passed through by the consumer (AGS state -> variant tables, per-group output directory, unsafe-render flag). `bar_mappings.states` is the fixed state -> variant resolution table: `make validate-icons` requires every value to name a variant in the same group, but never treats it as an editing surface. This repository ships the rest as data and does not interpret it

variant_entry.name: string — REQUIRED, unique within the group; the frozen selector a consumer asks for and the value side of `bar_mappings.states`
variant_entry.state: string — OPTIONAL state key this row draws (`wifi-full`, `low`, ...). Defaults to `name`. Required when the group declares `styles`, because a row is then one cell of the `state x style` grid. Unique per `(state, style)` pair within the group
variant_entry.style: string — OPTIONAL style this row draws, one of the group's `styles`. Required when the group declares `styles`; absent means the implicit `default` style. It is a redraw axis, not a state
variant_entry.template: string — REQUIRED path to the SVG RELATIVE TO THE GROUP'S TEMPLATE ROOT (`templates_root/<template_dir>`, where `template_dir` defaults to "."): forward slashes, no leading `/`, no `..`. The consumer joins it under that root — not under the mapping file's directory. Several variants may name the SAME template (one canonical drawing rendered with different params), including a row re-exported from another group, as `capture-tool/mic` re-exports the bar microphone art
variant_entry.output: string — REQUIRED; the rendered file name stem the consumer writes. A bare file name: no path separators, no `..`, no placeholder. It stays explicit and unchanged by this contract: for a group serving more than one surface the runtime derives `<stem>@<surface>.svg` mechanically from this stem; that artifact-naming rule is a runtime/platform concern, not a row in this repository
variant_entry.surface: string — OPTIONAL per-variant override of the effective surface, one of the group's `serves` values. Use it when the variant is not on the group's default layer: a variant that paints its own filled container (`solid`)
variant_entry.color_mappings: object — OPTIONAL per-variant token map, highest priority in the merge. It carries the row's params (`OPACITY_*`) and the variant role pins that are GENUINE TINTS (accent-on, caution, on-container for self-painted art). A pin that resolves to the same value the variant already inherits is dead data and fails the gate

surface_classes.description: The composition layer a glyph is drawn for. It is the missing datum behind the legacy `colorN` pins: the same carrier index is fine on a panel and wrong over the wallpaper. A group declares its default surface and the surfaces it serves; a variant overrides the surface only when it is not on the group's default layer. The surface is a render dimension, never a variant naming convention — that is what retires the `system-*` rows.

contract.wallpaper: Composited directly over the wallpaper (floating bar glyph, full-screen wallpaper button). Glyph ink MUST resolve to `on_backdrop`. Decorative accents may use `primary`/`tertiary`/`error`, but the shape must still carry the state when they miss contrast.
contract.dark-glass: On a translucent sheet, `alpha(surface*, ~0.9)` over a transparent window. Use the on-surface / on-container family for that sheet (`on_surface`, `on_surface_variant`, `on_primary`, `on_primary_container`, ...). `on_backdrop` is wrong here: no wallpaper band is behind the glyph.
contract.solid: On an opaque surface, field, or a container the variant paints itself. Use the on-surface / on-container family for that surface. `on_backdrop` is wrong here for the same reason as dark-glass.

surface_classes.surface_ink_rule: For every surface a row renders on (its own `surface`, else the group's default): if the row does not pin the ink token, the inherited ink must satisfy that surface's contract (`wallpaper` -> `on_backdrop`, `dark-glass`/`solid` -> a role in the on-surface family). A variant-level ink pin is an explicit tint and is not re-derived; it must still sit on a declared surface. A group's own `COLOR_FOREGROUND` pin is checked against the group's default `surface`.

placeholder_vocabulary.description: Placeholders are the only variable part of a template. The vocabulary is a contract: renaming a token breaks every consumer that supplies it, so a rename is a MAJOR change even though no file moved.
placeholder_vocabulary.syntax: {{NAME}} — exactly two opening braces, the name, two closing braces, no whitespace inside, nothing else on the token
rules: Every token used by any .svg under a group's template directory MUST be declared in that group's `color_mappings` (or a variant override), or in `icons/mappings/defaults.yaml` (the group-independent vocabulary).
Every mapping VALUE follows its token's family: COLOR_* is a declared role or `#rrggbb`, OPACITY_* is a numeric literal in [0, 1].
Declaring a token no SVG uses is allowed (forward compatibility); `make validate-icons` reports it, it does not fail the tag.
No defaults, filters, conditionals or nesting inside a token.
A token is substituted by the CONSUMER at render time. No rendered SVG, no generated icon index and no palette state is ever committed here (spine AD-11).
`output` values and mapping keys may not contain `{{`.

validation.make validate: The envelope: valid JSON, integer `schema_major`, and the `shape` / `placeholder_vocabulary` sections present (scripts/validate-catalog.py).
make validate-icons: `mappings/` holds exactly one group map (`icons.yaml`) plus the vocabulary (`defaults.yaml`); any other `*.yaml` fails, because the consumer loads one file and a split is a second source of truth
`schema_major` is exactly 2 — the checker implements one version and asserts it, so the contract file and the checker are bumped together
every `template:` in `icons.yaml` resolves to a real file under `icons/templates/<template_dir>/` (several variants may share one template)
every token used by a template is declared in `defaults.yaml` or that group's / variant's `color_mappings`, and the token name is a legal `COLOR_*` / `OPACITY_*` name

every COLOR_* value is a role declared in `mappings/vocabulary.json` or a `#rrggbb` literal; `colorN` and aliases fail unless they are an exact entry in `phase_a_legacy_baseline`, and a baseline entry that no longer matches a live pin also fails (shrink-only ratchet)
every OPACITY_* value is a numeric literal in [0, 1]; a role as an opacity, or a number as a colour, fails the family check
`mappings/vocabulary.json` declares 50 Material roles plus `on_backdrop`, unique, with its source note and the three surface classes
every group declares a valid `surface`, every `serves` entry is a valid surface and `serves` contains `surface`, and every variant `surface` is one the group serves
the surface-ink rule holds for every row: wallpaper -> `on_backdrop`, dark-glass/solid -> the on-surface family when the row does not pin the ink (a pin is a tint)
`styles` is declared per group, unique, and every variant of a styled group declares a `style` from it; `(state, style)` is unique within the group
every `bar_mappings.states` value names a variant in the same group, and a variant's declared `state` resolves through the table on the default style
a variant pin that resolves to the same value it already inherits is dead data and fails (pins are tints, not restatements)
`mappings/ROLE-MIGRATION.md` names every group and variant in `icons.yaml` (the reviewed proposal cannot silently miss new art)
every SVG under `icons/templates/` parses as XML
every `variant.name` is unique within its group
every `output` is a bare file name and every `template` stays inside the templates root
reported_not_failed: a token declared for a group but unused by its templates (forward compatibility)
a `(state, style)` grid cell a styled group does not draw (a consumer blanks loudly rather than inventing art)
validation.make validate-content: The content class: `content/wallpapers/wallpapers.tar.gz` holds a top-level `default.png`, every `*.theme` is non-empty, and no archive member escapes the archive root.
validation.new_work: schema_major 2 lands with the canonical-art collapse (REQ-149 slice 3): 123 -> 106 templates, 142 -> 130 rows. The 12 `system-*` rows retire because the surface dimension replaces them; the 3 panel ladders, the network ladders in the `default`/`rounded` styles and `volume/{medium,max}` collapse to one canonical template each plus `OPACITY_*` params; three byte-identical duplicates are single-sourced. Every collapsed/deleted/re-pointed variant was rendered before and after with the pinned renderer and holds its geometry and effective paint; the harness is `tickets/req-149-icon-schema-v2/verify-collapse.py`.
